key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation in perovskites from early time-series data, enabling explainable stability prediction for unseen samples.
engineering_relevance: This approach could shorten solar-cell materials screening by replacing some slow ageing tests with faster, data-driven stability forecasts.
method: Collected a diverse dataset of 167 metal halide perovskites under heat and light stress.
Featurized more than 86,000 photoluminescence spectra with a physics-informed model.
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict PL intensity during degradation and identify stability descriptors.
evidence_signal: The model was evaluated on unseen samples, generalized across material groups, and outperformed baseline benchmarks according to the abstract.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and diversity of the stress-testing dataset, so transfer to new perovskite chemistries or experimental conditions should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
